title: PLA Southern Theater Command Launches 'Combat Readiness Patrols' at Scarborough Shoal Following USCG Midgett Joint Exercise; Teodoro: Manila Under 'Severe Threat'
detail: China's PLA Southern Theater Command executed 'combat readiness patrols' in the territorial waters and airspace of Scarborough Shoal (Huangyan Island) on June 1, 2026, one day after the Philippines and the United States completed their five-day joint maritime presence operation involving USCG Midgett (WMSL-757) and PCG BRP Melchora Aquino near the feature (May 28–31). China's Coast Guard simultaneously conducted separate 'law enforcement patrols' near the shoal. The PLA stated such patrols 'serve as an effective countermeasure to cope with all sorts of rights violations and provocative acts' — explicitly framing them as a direct response to the USCG–PCG bilateral presence exercise. Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro, speaking from the sidelines of the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, declared: 'We have no choice but really to be resilient and to stand up against Chinese aggression,' and confirmed that Manila remains under 'severe threat' from China territorially and politically despite recent US–China diplomatic improvements following a Trump–Xi summit in May 2026. The June 1 PLA STC patrols follow the 16+ vessel CCG–militia dual-ring perimeter maintained at Scarborough on May 31 and constitute the most direct Chinese military counter-signal following the USCG–PCG bilateral presence operations at the disputed feature. China's Xiang Yang Hong 33 research vessel entered Day 26 of unauthorized presence near Pag-asa Island on June 1, with Beijing's UNCLOS Article 246 diplomatic silence extending to Day 21 — the longest unanswered Philippine diplomatic instrument under the Marcos administration.

title: China Deploys CCG Patrols East of Taiwan in Response to Japan-Philippines Maritime Boundary Delimitation Talks; Beijing Calls Talks 'Completely Illegal, Null and Void'
detail: China's Coast Guard conducted 'law enforcement patrols' in waters east of Taiwan on June 1, 2026, in direct response to Japan and the Philippines formally announcing the launch of maritime boundary delimitation talks during a summit between Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in Tokyo on May 29, 2026. The two countries agreed to negotiate the boundaries of their respective exclusive economic zones and continental shelves 'in accordance with international law.' China's Coast Guard declared the patrol 'a necessary action taken in response to Japan and the Philippines unilaterally announcing the initiation of maritime boundary delimitation negotiations in the waters east of China's Taiwan island,' urging both countries to 'immediately cease all illegal actions that infringe upon China's sovereign rights and interests.' China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning characterized the talks as 'completely illegal and invalid' and 'null and void,' claiming the relevant waters overlap with China's claimed EEZ and continental shelf. Taiwan's Foreign Ministry countered that 'China has no right to interfere in Taiwan's territorial sovereignty and sovereign rights over its relevant maritime areas.' The Japan–Philippines maritime boundary delimitation talks represent a deepening of the bilateral alliance following the Reciprocal Access Agreement (entered into force September 2025) and Japan's first overseas combat-capable JSDF deployment to the Philippines since WWII during Balikatan 2026. China's CCG patrols east of Taiwan extend Beijing's gray zone operations from the South China Sea into the western Pacific, creating a new front simultaneous with the ongoing Scarborough Shoal, Second Thomas Shoal, and Pag-asa Island standoffs.
